question.prompt: For certain real numbers \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c,\) the polynomial \[g(x)=x^3+ax^2+x+10\] has three distinct roots, and each root of \(g(x)\) is also a root of the polynomial \[ \begin{aligned} &f(x)=x^4+x^3+bx^2 \\ &\quad {}+100x+c. \end{aligned} \] What is \(f(1)?\)

solutions.title: A linear quotient and matching coefficients
solutions.explanation:
The three distinct roots shared by \(f\) and \(g\) make \(g\) a factor of \(f\). Both polynomials have leading coefficient \(1\), and their degrees differ by one, so for some real number \(q\),
\[
f(x)=(x-q)(x^3+ax^2+x+10).
\]
Expanding gives
\[
f(x)=x^4+(a-q)x^3+(1-qa)x^2+(10-q)x-10q.
\]
Compare the coefficient of \(x\) with the given polynomial:
\[
10-q=100\quad\Longrightarrow\quad q=-90.
\]
The coefficient of \(x^3\) then gives
\[
a-q=1\quad\Longrightarrow\quad a+90=1\quad\Longrightarrow\quad a=-89.
\]
Now evaluate the factored expression at \(x=1\):
\[
f(1)=(1+90)(1-89+1+10)=91(-77)=\boxed{-7007}.
\]
The answer is choice C.
